approach.summary: Add a `json` bool flag to cmdStats. Once the runs are sorted, and only when the flag is set, a new helper printStatsJSON builds {runs, totals}. It marshals the document with json.MarshalIndent("", " ") as `status --json` does, prints it to stdout and returns ExitOK. The text path is not touched. Each run uses one struct whose fields are pointers without omitempty (id stays a plain string). A damaged run therefore keeps every key, with null values and its reason in `damaged`. A readable run fills every pointer and leaves `damaged` nil. The totals follow the rules of the text loop, with two lower-bound booleans. The usage line and the README row gain `--json`. The existing stats test gets a JSON pass on the same fixture that checks the null keys of the damaged run.

alternatives.why_not: The task asks for null, not zero. A zero would look like real data.

alternatives.why_not: It drops keys: real zeros disappear from readable runs, and damaged runs lose keys.

steps.title: Add --json to shogun stats
steps.objective: With --json, print the stats runs and totals as one JSON document, using the damaged-run shape the task requires. The text output does not change.
actions: Before editing, build the current HEAD binary to a path outside the repo (e.g. /tmp/shogun-before). Prepare a static runs directory outside the repo that holds a few runs, one of them damaged. Either copy an existing .shogun/runs or make a few run dirs by hand, one with an invalid state.json. Capture `/tmp/shogun-before stats --dir <that dir>` to /tmp/stats-before.txt.
In cmd/shogun/stats.go, add `encoding/json` to the imports. In cmdStats, add `asJSON := fs.Bool("json", false, "print runs and totals as JSON")` next to the --dir flag.
In cmdStats, right after the sort.Slice line (line 59) and before the `len(runs) == 0` check, add `if *asJSON { return a.printStatsJSON(runs) }`. Leave every other line of the text path as it is.

Add the JSON types to stats.go. statsRunJSON: ID string `json:"id"` and Status string `json:"status"`, plus these pointer fields, all without omitempty:
- Mode, Planner, Reviewer *string (`mode`, `planner`, `reviewer`)
- Attempts *int (`attempts`)
- ActiveSeconds *float64 (`active_seconds`)
- InputTokens, CacheReadTokens, CacheWriteTokens, OutputTokens, ReasoningTokens *int64 (`input_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`)
- CostUSD *float64 (`cost_usd`)
- Usage *string (`usage`)
- Damaged *string (`damaged`)
statsTotalsJSON: ByStatus map[string]int `by_status`, Damaged int `damaged`, Attempts int, ActiveSeconds float64, the five int64 token sums and CostUSD float64 (these use the same keys as the run fields), SpendLowerBound bool `spend_lower_bound` and UsageLowerBound bool `usage_lower_bound`. The document struct: Runs []statsRunJSON `runs` and Totals statsTotalsJSON `totals`.

Add `func (a *app) printStatsJSON(runs []runStats) int` with a one-line comment in the file's style. Start with a non-nil empty Runs slice and an empty ByStatus map.
- Damaged run (r.st == nil): increment Damaged, set reason := r.damaged, and append {ID: r.id, Status: "damaged", Damaged: &reason}. Leave every other pointer nil.
- Readable run: set c := r.st.Counters and status := string(r.st.Status), increment ByStatus[status], take u := r.usage(), and set anyPartial when u != "ok". Make local copies of mode, planner, reviewer, u and the counters, and append a statsRunJSON with every pointer set to those copies and Damaged nil. Add the counters to the totals exactly as lines 83-90 do.
After the loop, set SpendLowerBound = Damaged > 0 and UsageLowerBound = anyPartial || Damaged > 0. Marshal with json.MarshalIndent(doc, "", " "), Fprintln the result to a.stdout and return ExitOK.

In cmd/shogun/main.go:97, change `shogun stats [--dir d]` to `shogun stats [--dir d] [--json]` and keep the description column aligned. In README.md:237, change the trailing ``; `--dir` `` to ``; `--dir`; `--json` prints the same as JSON ``.
Build the changed tree to /tmp/shogun-after. Run `stats --dir` on the same static directory, without --json, into /tmp/stats-after.txt, and diff it against the before capture.

verification.expected: `diff /tmp/stats-before.txt /tmp/stats-after.txt` prints nothing (R-004.C2). `go build ./...` succeeds and `gofmt -l cmd/shogun` prints nothing.

risks.risk: Pointers to a loop variable or a shared local get aliased, so every run object shows the last run's values.
risks.mitigation: Declare the per-run copies inside the loop body; Go 1.22+ also scopes loop variables per iteration. The S-002 test checks values that differ between runs (approved vs paused usage).

risks.risk: A run in the captured directory changes between the before and after captures, which gives a false diff.
risks.mitigation: Capture from a static copy outside any live workspace.

steps.title: Test stats --json on the existing fixture
steps.objective: Prove the shape and contents of the JSON document, including the null keys of the damaged run. Also prove that the text output is unchanged and that the command wrote nothing.
actions: In TestStatsCountsEveryRunAndFlagsMissingUsage, add the new checks after the existing state.json comparison (line 77) and change no existing line. Run `code, out, errs = runCLI(t, ws, "stats", "--json")`. Require ExitOK and empty errs, and require that out contains neither "RUN" nor "total:".

Decode out with a json.Decoder into struct{ Runs []map[string]any `json:"runs"`; Totals map[string]any `json:"totals"` }, and require that a second Decode returns io.EOF. Add `encoding/json` and `io` to the imports.
Require 5 runs in id order. Check the approved run's values against R-002.C1 (numbers decode as float64; damaged is present and nil). Check that the paused run's usage is "unknown".

Find 20260927-000003-c. Require status "damaged" and a non-empty string in `damaged`. For each of mode, planner, reviewer, attempts, active_seconds, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_usd and usage, require that the key is present (`v, ok := m[k]; ok`) and that v == nil.
Require that every run object has exactly the same 15 keys, and that `damaged` is present and nil on the four readable runs (R-002.C3).
Check the totals against R-003.C1, and check that spend_lower_bound and usage_lower_bound are both true (R-003.C2).
Read the approved run's state.json again and compare it with `before` (R-005.C1).

`git diff cmd/shogun/stats_test.go` shows only added lines (the imports and the new block). The existing text assertions are therefore unmodified, and they pass in V-002 (R-004.C1).

questions.question: With --json and an empty runs directory, should stats print a JSON document with an empty runs list and zero totals, or keep today's behaviour (a 'no runs in …' note on stderr and nothing on stdout)?
questions.why: The task does not cover the empty case, and a consumer that parses stdout would break on empty output.
questions.impact: It only decides whether the `if *asJSON` check comes before or after the `len(runs) == 0` check in cmdStats.
options: Print {"runs": [], "totals": {…zeros, lower bounds false}} and no stderr note
Keep the stderr note and print nothing on stdout
questions.proposed_assumption: Print the JSON document with an empty runs array and zero totals (no stderr note), as in-1 decided; this is easy to switch.
